newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH LEAGUE FIXTURE ALTERED FOR KOEPKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH LEAGUE FIXTURE ALTERED FOR KOEPKE.

text.p: Marseille's French league match at Montpellier next week has been rescheduled to allow their German goalkeeper Andreas Koepke time to join his country for their World Cup qualifier against Northern Ireland on August 20.
Montpellier were to have hosted the match, third of the league season, on Sunday, August 17, the day Koepke was due to join Berti Vogts' Germany squad in Belfast.
The French league (LNF) authorities have brought the match forward to Saturday, August 16, when six other games are scheduled. There are two games on Friday, August 15.
The French Football Federation (FFF), however, does not wish to be as accomodating as the LNF with the Germans.
Vogts has asked the FFF if Germany could play France in a friendly in Paris on November 15 if they win their World Cup qualifying group and avoid playoffs scheduled for that night.

The Germans would be looking to replace Croatia, scheduled to meet the World Cup hosts in the friendly in St Etienne, if the Croatians are forced into a playoff for a place in the 1998 finals instead.
A FFF spokesman said: "We have made it clear (to Germany) that, in the current state of things, we can not envisage playing them before the 1998 World Cup.
"For now it's Croatia. We'll wait until September 6."
Croatia, third in group one, four points behind leaders Denmark, are at home to Bosnia on September 6. They also visit Denmark four days later and Slovenia in their last match on October 11.
